subject: Performance SLO / Customer-led load test coordination (FinWise)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@finwise.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs and next steps for customer-led load test

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Summary of targets you mentioned on the call:
- Latency: p50 <= 150 ms, p95 <= 350 ms (end-to-end token generation)
- Throughput: sustained 100 requests/second with bursts to 200rps for 10m windows
- Concurrency: ~20 concurrent sessions/steady-state streams
- Streaming: must support token-level streaming (SSE or chunked HTTP). You noted half-second expected token-latency target for interactive flows.

Customer-led load test ask: please share your k6/Locust scripts (or a runbook) and a proposed test window. We can provide a short-lived test API key and IP allowlist ranges to whitelist. Our suggested approach:
1) You run the k6 script from your infra against our staging endpoint (we'll provide key + allowlist).
2) Start with a ramp to 100rps over 15m, hold for 30m, then a 10m spike to 200rps.
3) Enable streaming tests in a separate run to validate chunked responses and SSE behavior.

Action items for Redwood (assigned):
- Provide test API key and staging host (Logan)
- Share IP ranges to whitelist (Rishi)
- Prepare temporary rate-limit bump and monitoring dashboard (Marissa)

Can you share your k6 script and confirm a preferred test window next week (US mornings are ideal for us)?

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs and next steps for customer-led load test

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear recap. Alex and I chatted and we can run the load tests from our infra and share the scripts. Attaching our preliminary k6 script (finwise_k6_test.js) and a short plan.

Notes / questions:
- We'll start with the ramp/hold/spike you suggested.
- For streaming: our current k6 runner uses chunked responses; can you confirm whether your staging endpoint supports SSE and chunked HTTP equally (we prefer SSE for token events, but can adapt).
- Test window: would like to propose Tue Dec 1, 09:00-12:00 PT. If that works for you we'll register the run and run 2 validation passes.

We'll need the following from you to proceed:
1) A staging API key with the same per-token model behavior as production (test key ok).
2) IP ranges to whitelist so our runner isn't dropped mid-run.
3) A short list of sample prompts to use for representative latency (3-4 prompt templates).

Cheers,
Sarah Connor
Sr. Platform Engineer — FinWise

Attachments: finwise_k6_test.js, initial-runbook.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs and next steps for customer-led load test

Looping in a couple of operational details from our side. 

Rishi — can you confirm the CIDR we should provide to FinWise (we typically supply the egress ranges for the staging frontends and the LB)? Also please prepare a temporary rate-limit policy for this test (bump to allow 220rps for the staging key, enforce per-client concurrency limit at 250) so we don't hit global rate limiters.

Logan — I'll stand up the Grafana dashboard for the test (per-route latency, token breakdown, infra GPU utilization) and add alerting for error rates >1%. We'll include an eyeball channel in #prod-loadtests and schedule an SRE on-call for the window.

I recommend we ask FinWise to run a streaming-only pass as a separate run to avoid mixing metrics. Also: provide them with 3 sample prompts (we have a set for interactive chat, another for long completion). I can draft and share.

-M
Marissa Cole
Customer Success / Solutions

Thanks Rishi — CIDRs look good. Quick follow-up on streaming behavior: our token consumer expects Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream) with each token emitted as an event. Does your staging endpoint support SSE or should we use chunked transfer with JSON fragments? We prefer SSE for easier parsing.

Also confirming the proposed window Tue Dec 1, 09:00-12:00 PT. We will run two passes (functional ramp/hold/spike + streaming-only pass).

-Alex
